title: Bumplz: Physics Auto Battler Mobile Game
author: kfiler
selftext:
**What it is:** Bumplz is a physics auto-battler for iOS, built in Unity 6. You buy little creatures (Bumplz) in a shop, arrange them on a 3×3 grid, dress them in coats, then press **Bump**. Both teams get launched into a sealed chamber and smash into each other. No one aims anything: damage comes from real physics collisions, and a speed floor that keeps rising means every round eventually ends. A run is 15 wins before 5 losses. Right now there are 24 Bumplz across several factions and 3 tiers, plus 13 items with poison, burn, shields and on-hit effects. Modes: VS Computer, VS Friends (lobbies of up to 10, with battles streamed as replays) and VS World (you fight other players' saved "ghost" builds).

**How AI was used**

* **Code:** almost all of it was written with Claude Code. I direct, design and playtest.
* **Music:** Suno.
* **Art / models:** NanoBanana (image) -> Hunyuan (mesh & texture)

**The workflow (the part that might help others)**

1. **A docs "vault" instead of one giant design doc.** Each system gets its own small note (`design/shop.md`, `design/balance.md`…), every decision gets an ADR (24 so far), and every session ends with a dated note plus a [`current.md`](http://current.md) "where we are" file. The agent reads [`current.md`](http://current.md) and the one note it needs, not the whole project. This was the biggest single improvement. Without it, every new chat re-learned the project and re-broke things.
2. **Hard-won rules go in CLAUDE.md.** Example: "stats belong to the Bumpl, never the grid spot". Poison was staying on a grid spot after its Bumpl moved, and the next occupant inherited it. Once a bug class like that is written down as a rule, it stops coming back.
3. **Compile checks without opening Unity.** A script compiles the C# against Unity's real assemblies, so the agent can verify its own changes headlessly before claiming they work.
4. **"Compiled" ≠ "works".** The agent can't play the game. Every session note says *compiled, not play-tested* until I've actually played it on a device. Physics games especially surprise you.
5. **Coaching from my phone.** I send an instruction from my phone, the agent makes the change and drops a build request file, and a watcher on a Mac mini builds and uploads to TestFlight. About 30 minutes later I'm testing it on my phone.

**Lesson from the latest balance pass:** I had the agent audit every unit against one stat budget. Because buffs stack every round, most grants turned out 3–10× too strong. It also found that "buff N random teammates" was hitting the *whole* team because of a targeting bug. AI is great at this kind of systematic audit once you give it a written budget to check against.

Happy to answer questions about the setup. Feedback on the game feel is very welcome too.

*Android:* [*https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.loxodonta.bumplz*](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.loxodonta.bumplz) *(Android is still in testing. Sign up at* [*bumplz.com*](http://bumplz.com) *if you want to be added to the play tester list.)*
